title: Swath scanning laser altimeter
description: DTU Space is heavily involved in ESA’s airborne satellite calibration and validation campaigns in polar regions. To secure the DTU Space instrument package is living up to the needs for validation of current (ESA CryoSat, NASA ICESat-2) and to exploit the precision of future dual-frequency satellite missions (such as Copernicus high-priority candidate mission CRISTAL) it is of vital importance to purchase a swath scanning laser altimeter. The laser altimeter shall be a compact system adapted to a mid-sized aircraft and capable of measuring the surface of sea ice, land ice and ocean water. As the laser scanner system will be used together with airborne radar altimeters, the laser scanner shall, as a minimum, be operable within ranges of 300-1000 m for reflective targets of ≥ 10%. The purchase is a vital part of the nationally funded project Greenland Integrated Observing System (GIOS) and contributes to the development of a new research infrastructure providing a much-required sustained and long-term observation network of the central climate around Greenland representing not only entire Greenland but also a climate gradient representing the Arctic as a whole.

title: Satellite imagery for in-shore ice analysis in Greenland
description: DMI monitors and reports routinely on sea ice and iceberg conditions near shore and inshore in South Greenland for direct support and guidance of local shipping. The suite of local ships ranges from com-mercial, passenger and coast guard ships to small individual and sail boats. The occurrence of sea ice and icebergs is a hazard or obstacle to local shipping. It has been procedure for years to notify local shipping about difficult ice before they actually enter such areas so appropriate bridge decisions can made. The primary area of interest is within 59°45’N-62°00N and 42°50’W-48°30’W. The standard products based on the helicopter recce are the following: - Ice report in plain language - Photo series of ice conditions at selected or critical positions or annotated satellite imagery. Most often .jpg files with symbols and explanations of ice conditions. - Direct ice advisory to ships via HF radio Satellite data recorded in visual wavelength in resolutions of 15-20 m or better are very valuable for the inshore mapping program however fog, cloud cover and winter darkness is a significant limitation and imagery recorded with Synthetic Aperture Radar is a necessary complimentary datasource. Near real time delivery of data is critical for the inshore program however access to data within a couple of hours turned out to be acceptable.

title: Autonomous floats for the ARGO program
description: Argo is a global real-time ocean observing network with a fleet of autonomous floats measuring the properties of seawater and sending data in real time via satellite communications. The floats can regu-late their buoyancy and therefore collect measurements of profiles of water properties. This makes them unique compared to other sustained observation systems which measure only at fixed depths (buoys or remote sensing). The program represents a fleet of about 4000 autonomous floats, deployed all over the world ocean. They carry an array of sensors with the core being temperature, and salinity, while other sensors are often added to cover other parameters such as dissolved oxygen, phytoplankton fluorescence, or-ganic matter fluorescence, nitrate, particle scattering and irradiance. The data is made freely available to all via coordinated global ARGO data centers. Just as weather balloons provide profiles of atmos-pheric conditions for weather forecasting, the ARGO program delivers ocean properties for monitor-ing and forecasting ocean conditions (operational modelling) and also supporting climate research and modelling. Technical University of Denmark (DTU) has initiated Denmark participation in ARGO via a Research in-frastructure grant from the Ministry of Higher Education and Science. The initiative has now been tak-en over by Danish Centre for Marine Research (DCMR), the secretariate of which is at DTU. DCMR is a national virtual centre funded by the national budget, with representation from all institutions in-volved in marine research in the Kingdom of Denmark.

title: Framework Agreement regarding High Bandwidth Low Latency SATCOM
description: Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organisation (DALO) is executing a tender of High bandwidth Low Latency SATCOM to be used in the Danish Defence. The Danish Defence often operates outside of traditionel internet infrastructure. Current acces to the internet in such locations is obtained via SATCOM, based on geostationary satellite constellations at a distance of more than 35.000 kilometres from Earth. This very long distance communication limits both latency and the bandwidth of such systems. With increased need for internet access, pertaining to administrative tasks and crew Wi-Fi, a new SATCOM system with low latency and high bandwidth is required. It is expected that the data based communication will increase in the future, as the service becomes more widely used in the Danish Defence. The Danish Defence operates all over the world both on land and at sea. DALO therefore needs a solution with global coverage. However, DALO is also aware that the different solutions on the market at present can not quarantee global coverage. Therefore, to maximise the connectivity, DALO whishes to acquire two solutions of High Bandwidth Low Latency SATCOM. It is not the plan that both solutions of High Bandwidth Low Latency SATCOM will be installed and used on the different platforms. However, certain platforms might have both solutions installed. The solution is intended to be used on both stationary and moving platforms, and as such it is required to be able to function on-the-move. The solution will be subjected to harsh weather conditions of the Arctic with low temperatures, high winds and rough seas, but also warm sub-tropic climate. As the vessels of the Royal Danish Navy will periodically be docked for maintenance for extended periods of time, DALO whishes a solution where the connection can be frozen/paused. The framework agreement will concist of Terminals and Subscriptions (Airtime) as well as training, repair-services and spare parts.

title: Udbud af Host broadcast ydelser til Danmarks EU-formandskab 2025
description: Danmark skal i andet halvår af 2025 (1. juli 2025 – 31. december 2025) varetage formandskabet for EU’s ministerråd med en omfattende mødeaktivitet på dansk jord til følge. Der vil således i denne periode skulle afholdes en række uformelle ministermøder, et møde mellem regeringen og EU-Kommissionen, en åbningsceremoni, samt to topmøder. Disse møder forventes at tiltrække mediebevågenhed, og derfor skal formandskabet have en officiel leverandør af TV-tjenester; en host broadcaster. Host broadcasteren skal levere TV-signaler og -optagelser til akkrediterede TV-stationer samt på bestilling til andre TV-stationer af de større møder i Danmark. Kontrakten vil omfatte levering af host broadcast (HBC)-ydelser, herunder den nødvendige teknik, opstilling, montering og installation samt servicering og betjening af det benyttede udstyr. HBC-opgaven vil bl.a. indebære at etablere, producere og levere TV-dækning i lyd og billeder til Europe by Satellite (EbS) og ti anvendelse af alle akkrediterede medier, at levere direkte transmission fra doorsteps og officielle pressekonferencer ved ministermøder, topmøder og Kommissionens besøg, samt at levere den tekniske infrastruktur, inkl. opsætning og nedtagning, som er nødvendig for opgavens tilvejebringelse. title: Submarine Cable project consultancies DPS
description: This DPS concerns consultancies relating to Polar Connect step 1. Polar Connect is a submarine fiber cable project with a shortest route between and East Asia starting from Norway going north of Greenland to North America and onwards to Asia. The cable is intended to be a hybrid cable that will support generic telecommunications connectivity, as well as supporting research using smart cable technologies. The Polar Connect step 1 runs for 3 years from January 2025 to December 2027 and is aimed to achieve several objectives in the areas described below. • Engagement with stakeholders interested in securing global connectivity and providing access to an innovative research instrument made of sensors along the subsea cable. • Detailed mapping of the Arctic Ocean, which starts with preparing pre-survey of the route, mission planning considering the critical weather conditions and costs, three survey missions, and the analysis of the survey data. • Technical planning and design activities, including route planning, planning of the resilience, determination of the optimal locations of potential cable landing sites and branching units, including security and access control, environmental impact, permitting and regulatory compliance, collaboration with local authorities, emergency response and repair, remote monitoring and control systems, and back-up communication systems. • Sensor technology planning, analysis of available technologies for cable sensing and their contributions for security-, integrity-, scientific- and environmental monitoring. It is foreseen that there will be consultancies needed for several areas.

title: PreCommercial Procurement for the Customisation/Preoperationalisation of Water management Innovations from Space for European Climate Resilience
description: This PCP (Pre-Commercial Procurement) is a cross-border joint procurement of R&D services to reinforce public demand-driven innovation in end-user services in the area of Climate Change Adaptation through data-driven water management. The to-be-developed solutions are expected to achieve TRL 7-8. The PCP should deliver successful, innovative and fully tested product(s) and/or service(s) that meet the common needs of the Public Buyer Group (PBG) to procure research services, develop innovative marketable solutions, speed up the time-to-market and provide best value for money. More concretely, the common needs of the public buyer group are as follows. PCP WISE aims to develop smart, sustainable solutions to improve water management and climate resiliency by monitoring the ‘Soil-Water-Vegetation (SWV) System’. Market entities are challenged to design and develop a solution that achieves this by using and combining earth observation data and environmental data on the SWV-system. This to-be-developed integrated water intelligence information product/service aims to help decision-makers manage major challenges resulting from climate change, such as floods, droughts, wildfires, heat stress and infrastructure risks in both urban and rural areas. The PCP WISE project includes 5 use cases that serve as practical testing scenarios where innovative solutions must demonstrate their effectiveness in real-world conditions. They represent the diverse geographic and climatic contexts of the European continent that provide the reference framework against which the innovations are validated for relevance, resilience and impact. PCP WISE contractors are challenged by designing and developing a solution that is applicable and scalable to tackle all 5 use cases. After evaluation of the tenders received, the PCP will be implemented by means of awarding a Framework Agreement where contractors are developing the solution in competition. It includes call-offs for Specific Contracts for Phase 1: Solution Design, Phase 2: Prototype Development, and Phase 3: Validation and demonstration of the solutions. This project receives funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme under grant agreement number No. 101182917 and selected under the HORIZONCL62024 GOVERNANCE015, topic: Customisation/preoperationalisation of prototypes enduser services in the area Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation, with a budget of around €12 million earmarked for the R&D phases during the implementation of the PCP instrument. However, the European Union does not participate as a contracting authority in the procurement.

title: Laser Frequency Comb for 2ES
description: DTU will like to buy a Laser Frequency Comb for 2ES (The Second Earth Spectrograph). The Second Earth Spectrograph (2ES) is a next-generation extreme-precision radial velocity spectro-graph that will be installed at the MPG/ESO 2.2m Telescope on La Silla, Chile (Southern Hemisphere). 2ES will be dedicated to a > 5-year observing program with access to the majority (2/3) of the tele-scope time with the goal of discovering temperate terrestrial Earth-mass planets in the habitable zone around the brightest solar-type stars in the sky. In order to achieve the extreme precision needed for 2ES to complete its science objectives, a Laser Frequency Comb (LFC) calibration source is crucial in order to be able to calibrate the spectrograph to achieve the extreme precision of 10 cm/s over many years of operation. The LFC must cover the entire wavelength range of 2ES (370 nm to 870 nm) and have comb lines at appropriate spacing (see requirements) and have extreme stability (see requirements). The LFC must be able to function in a as-tronomical observing environment, be remotely operatable and be also to sustain a significant uptime at the astronomical telescope.

title: Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance
description: This tender concerns a contract for Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance. The overall purpose is to limit and mitigate pollution in the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven) section 5) by performing airborne maritime pollution control and to enforce the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven). Further information about the characteristics of the airborne maritime pollution control can be obtained from the following sources: — The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea; UNCLOS; — The Bonn-Agreement; — The Helsinki Convention (HELCOM); — The DENGERNETH Plan; — The SWEDENGER Plan; — The Copenhagen Agreement. The supplier enters this agreement with DALO as the contracting party, and the inherent tasks are performed by the Danish Defence. The responsibility for pollution response and counter-pollution surveillance of the marine environement rests with the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness. title: Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya
description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment will align with and leverage the resulting business, data, application, technology and security architectures to guide the design and implementation of WRIMS, while supporting the operationalisation of the EA, particularly in systems integration, interoperability, data governance, ICT infrastructure and cybersecurity. title: Framework Agreement regarding High Bandwidth Low Latency SATCOM
description: Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organisation (DALO) has executed a tender of High bandwidth Low Latency SATCOM to be used in the Danish Defence. The Danish Defence often operates outside of traditionel internet infrastructure. Current acces to the internet in such locations is obtained via SATCOM, based on geostationary satellite constellations at a distance of more than 35.000 kilometres from Earth. This very long distance communication limits both latency and the bandwidth of such systems. With increased need for internet access, pertaining to administrative tasks and crew Wi-Fi, a new SATCOM system with low latency and high bandwidth is required. It is expected that the data based communication will increase in the future, as the service becomes more widely used in the Danish Defence. The Danish Defence operates all over the world both on land and at sea. DALO therefore needs a solution with global coverage. However, DALO is also aware that the different solutions on the market at present can not quarantee global coverage. Therefore, to maximise the connectivity, DALO whishes to acquire two solutions of High Bandwidth Low Latency SATCOM. It is not the plan that both solutions of High Bandwidth Low Latency SATCOM will be installed and used on the different platforms. However, certain platforms might have both solutions installed. The solution is intended to be used on both stationary and moving platforms, and as such it is required to be able to function on-the-move. The solution will be subjected to harsh weather conditions of the Arctic with low temperatures, high winds and rough seas, but also warm sub-tropic climate. As the vessels of the Royal Danish Navy will periodically be docked for maintenance for extended periods of time, DALO whishes a solution where the connection can be frozen/paused. The framework agreement will concist of Terminals and Subscriptions (Airtime) as well as training, repair-services and spare parts.

title: Open Market Consultation (OMC) for a future Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) of R&D (research and development) services on the climate adaptation domain using space and EO (Earth Observation)-based information to prevent and mitigate water related crisis challenges to increase climate resilience in Europe – PCP WISE
description: This Prior Information Notice announces an OMC and provides early information in preparation for a future PCP carried out by the PCP WISE project (Public Procurement of Innovative Solutions for Water Management from Space). This project receives funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme under grant agreement number No. 101182917 and selected under the HORIZON-CL6-2024-GOVERNANCE-01-5, topic: Customisation/pre-operationalisation of prototypes end-user services in the area Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation (see EU Funding & Tenders Portal - https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/horizon-cl6-2024-governance-01-5), with a budget of €12 million earmarked for the R&D phases during the implementation of the PCP instrument. However, the European Union does not participate as a contracting authority in the procurement. PCP WISE aims to challenge the market to develop innovative solutions (up to TRL8) to improve water management, particularly in the fields of agriculture, urban climate resilience and planning, climate risk management and resilience to water-related natural disasters, using satellite based earth observation data, hydrological models, field data and artificial intelligence in order to provide intelligence on rural and urban soil-water-vegetation-system-conditions and related risks per sector. By leveraging space technology and environmental observation data, PCP WISE seeks to address critical challenges related to floods, fires, and infrastructure impacts both in rural and urban areas. This collaborative effort brings together public buyers, research institutions, and industry experts to create and implement advanced climate services that will enhance Europe's ability to adapt to and mitigate the effects of climate change. Therefore, it marks the start of an ambitious international collaboration dedicated to the sustainable management of water resources and the need to enlarge climate resilience across Europe. PCP WISE focuses on five distinct use cases, each addressing specific water-related challenges in different regions of Europe (North, South, West, and East) and geographical contexts (urban and rural) on flood, drought, subsidence, fire, or other concerns distinguishing between issues of a regular nature and those arising from crisis situations. For more information about the use cases, please see the OMC document. COMMUNICATION: Additional information can be obtained from the PCP WISE website* (PCP WISE: Pre-Commercial Procurement - Water management Innovation from Space for European climate resilience - https://pcp-wise.eu/open-market-consultation/) and/or the e-Procurement Platform** ( https://pcp-wise.tuttogare.it/index.php ). All the questions regarding the Open Market Consultation (OMC) should be asked through the PCP WISE OMC-Module in the aforementioned e-Procurement Platform. In the case of other issues (e.g. technical issues with the platform), the e-mail address of the Lead Procurer (see contact point) can be used. *The project’s official website will indicatively include information about the project, its Consortium, relevant news and events, matchmaking & networking opportunities, the PCP WISE’s Community Platform, the project’s social media and communication outputs as well as the OMC Documents. **Studio Amica’s e-Procurement Platform is a public procurement management software. Specifically the PCP-module of the platform will allow the PCP WISE Consortium to fully carry out the preliminary market consultation of PCP WISE and the future follow-up tender in compliance with the applicable European legislation. Finally, a Request for Information (RfI) questionnaire will provide the PCP WISE consortium with feedback from the market about its main challenge and use cases. Technology providers are invited to answer all the questions of the survey (one survey per company). The questionnaire should be filled out online and submitted via the following link: https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/PCP-WISE

title: Udbud af Host broadcast ydelser til Danmarks EU-formandskab 2025
description: Danmark skal i andet halvår af 2025 (1. juli 2025 – 31. december 2025) varetage formandskabet for EU’s ministerråd med en omfattende mødeaktivitet på dansk jord til følge. Der vil således i denne periode skulle afholdes en række uformelle ministermøder, et møde mellem regeringen og EU-Kommissionen, en åbningsceremoni, samt to topmøder. Disse møder forventes at tiltrække mediebevågenhed, og derfor skal formandskabet have en officiel leverandør af TV-tjenester; en host broadcaster. Host broadcasteren skal levere TV-signaler og -optagelser til akkrediterede TV-stationer samt på bestilling til andre TV-stationer af de større møder i Danmark. Kontrakten omfatter levering af host broadcast (HBC)-ydelser, herunder den nødvendige teknik, opstilling, montering og installation samt servicering og betjening af det benyttede udstyr. HBC-opgaven indebærer bl.a. at etablere, producere og levere TV-dækning i lyd og billeder til Europe by Satellite (EbS) og til anvendelse af alle akkrediterede medier, at levere direkte transmission fra doorsteps og officielle pressekonferencer ved ministermøder, topmøder og Kommissionens besøg, samt at levere den tekniske infrastruktur, inkl. opsætning og nedtagning, som er nødvendig for opgavens tilvejebringelse. Opgavens omfang er nærmere beskrevet i Kontrakten inkl. bilag hertil.

title: Bekendtgørelse om indgåelse af kontrakt om Integreret Marin Miljøovervågning
description: Kontrakten vedrører udviklingsprojektet Integreret Marin Miljøovervågning (IMM), som gennemføres af Styrelsen for Grøn Arealomlægning og Vandmiljø (SGAV). Formålet med IMM er at skabe en ny, omkostningseffektiv og skalérbar tilgang til indsamling af marine miljødata, som understøtter SGAVs marine overvågningsprogram, der er en del af det Nationale Overvågningsprogram for Vandmiljø og Natur (NOVANA). I IMM er der fokus på udvikling af nye måleteknologier (satellitter og målebøjer med in situ sensorer) samt videreudvikling af marin økosystemmodellering. Den tekniske løsning i IMM-projektet er centreret omkring marin økosystemmodellering, hvor der videreudvikles på SGAVs eksisterende marine modelkompleks bestående af i alt 11 modeller, som dækker de danske vandområder. Videreudviklingen indebærer integrering af data fra satellitter og målebøjer, som begge er nye og relevante teknologier ift. at levere marine miljødata. Desuden udvikles en løsning til en remote-sensing baseret kortlægning af marin vegetation, som bygger på en række tidligere studier og erfaringer.Kontrakten vedrører:1) Videreudviklingen af SGAVs marine modelkompleks inkl. integration af data fra satellit og målebøjer og operationalisering af modellerne.2) Kvalitetssikring af modelresultater med henblik på at kunne supplere SGAVs marine overvågningsprogram og levere data i henhold til EU-direktiver herunder Vandrammedirektivet, Havstrategidirektivet og Habitatdirektivet.3) Udvikling af remote-sensing baseret værktøj til national kortlægning af arealudbredelsen af marin undervandsvegetation, herunder udvikling af ny indikator i henhold til EU's Vandrammedirektiv.

title: Acquisition of a Secure Voice Communication System (VCS) and appertaining sustainment
description: 1) General description of the Contract: This contract award notice concerns DALO´s award of an Acquisition Contract, with a Sustainment Framework Agreement, for a VCS, including sustainment, i.e. development, implementation, maintenance and support during its life time (20 years). In order to facilitate both the acquisition and the sustainment, the procurement includes two main contractual agreements: an Acquisition Contract and a Sustainment Framework Agreement (together the “Contract”). These two agreements are mutually dependent and shall be seen together as a whole regulating the contractual relations between SAAB Danmark A/S and DALO. 2) The Acquisition Contract: The VCS facilitate voice communication between ground operational centers and other ground based operational entities as well as communication to and from aircrafts and vessels. The VCS will be used intensively and on a continuous basis (24/7/365) by the Danish Defence, including and foremost the Royal Danish Navy in relation to maritime surface surveillance and the Royal Danish Air Force for air surveillance, air battle management and Command and Control. Consequently, it is of utmost importance that the VCS and its functionalities operate with a high level of availability. Furthermore, in order for the VCS to efficiently contribute to the missions and operations within the span of tasks under the Danish Defence, the VCS have the following functionalities and characteristics: The VCS shall be scalable in terms of the number of centers, users and radios, the types of radios and services. The VCS is to be installed in Denmark on approx. 40 remote radio sites and 5 operational centers, one Test and School System, and one Reference System for reproduction of problems and test of software updates. Each radio site may have different types of radios allocated including HF, VHF, UHF and TETRA radios. Furthermore, the VCS shall integrate a voice recording system and a Cisco Call Manager based IP-telephone system operated by the Danish Defence (GFE). The VCS shall be security accredited to the classification level NATO SECRET and the Danish classification level HEMMELIGT. It is noted that NATO SECRET and HEMMELIGT is two individual accreditation approvals. The VCS’ primary function is to interconnect radios, telephone systems, intercom and public announcement systems. Besides the VCS’ primary function, the VCS shall be able to separate voice communication in minimum two security domains up to and including the classification levels NATO SECRET and HEMMELIGT. The VCS shall have a dedicated management system. VCS system components shall be capable of being used in all locations with an available IP infrastructure, including satellite links with high latency. The VCS shall be based on End-to-End IP architecture. TEMPEST modified equipment in the VCS shall be compliant to NATO SDIP-27. The VCS will be using DALO’s own government furnished equipment (GFE), including IP-WAN, cryptographic devices and Voice Recorders and shall be designed to integrate a wide range of different types of radios. TEMPEST modified equipment is also required at selected locations of the VCS. As part of the Contract, SAAB Danmark A/S shall deliver system documentation and technical maintenance documentation for the VCS. Furthermore, SAAB Danmark A/S shall deliver initial training and education for all kinds of users, including operators, system administrators and super-users. 3) The Sustainment Framework Agreement: During the expected lifetime of the VCS, DALO shall be able to acquire development and repair services and maintenance, including the possibility to acquire spare parts as well as off site and on site technical support. As part of these deliverables, SAAB Danmark A/S shall ensure that the system documentation and the technical maintenance documentation are kept updated continuously. On request, DALO shall be able to acquire training and education for all kinds of users, including operators, system administrators and super-users, remote radio site technicians as well as tailor made courses. Furthermore, SAAB Danmark A/S shall host a Reference system at a location in Denmark.

title: Autonomous floats for the ARGO program
description: Argo is a global real-time ocean observing network with a fleet of autonomous floats measuring the properties of seawater and sending data in real time via satellite communications. The floats can regu-late their buoyancy and therefore collect measurements of profiles of water properties. This makes them unique compared to other sustained observation systems which measure only at fixed depths (buoys or remote sensing). The program represents a fleet of about 4000 autonomous floats, deployed all over the world ocean. They carry an array of sensors with the core being temperature, and salinity, while other sensors are often added to cover other parameters such as dissolved oxygen, phytoplankton fluorescence, or-ganic matter fluorescence, nitrate, particle scattering and irradiance. The data is made freely available to all via coordinated global ARGO data centers. Just as weather balloons provide profiles of atmos-pheric conditions for weather forecasting, the ARGO program delivers ocean properties for monitor-ing and forecasting ocean conditions (operational modelling) and also supporting climate research and modelling. Technical University of Denmark (DTU) has initiated Denmark participation in ARGO via a Research in-frastructure grant from the Ministry of Higher Education and Science. The initiative has now been tak-en over by Danish Centre for Marine Research (DCMR), the secretariate of which is at DTU. DCMR is a national virtual centre funded by the national budget, with representation from all institutions in-volved in marine research in the Kingdom of Denmark.

title: Satellite imagery for in-shore ice analysis in Greenland
description: DMI monitors and reports routinely on sea ice and iceberg conditions near shore and inshore in South Greenland for direct support and guidance of local shipping. The suite of local ships ranges from com-mercial, passenger and coast guard ships to small individual and sail boats. The occurrence of sea ice and icebergs is a hazard or obstacle to local shipping. It has been procedure for years to notify local shipping about difficult ice before they actually enter such areas so appropriate bridge decisions can made. The primary area of interest is within 59°45’N-62°00N and 42°50’W-48°30’W. The standard products based on the helicopter recce are the following: - Ice report in plain language - Photo series of ice conditions at selected or critical positions or annotated satellite imagery. Most often .jpg files with symbols and explanations of ice conditions. - Direct ice advisory to ships via HF radio Satellite data recorded in visual wavelength in resolutions of 15-20 m or better are very valuable for the inshore mapping program however fog, cloud cover and winter darkness is a significant limitation and imagery recorded with Synthetic Aperture Radar is a necessary complimentary datasource. Near real time delivery of data is critical for the inshore program however access to data within a couple of hours turned out to be acceptable.

title: Markedsdialog om host broadcasting til det danske EU-formandskab 2025
description: Udenrigsministeriet inviterer til markedsdialog forud for kommende konkurrenceudsættelse af host broadcasting fra større møder i Danmark under det danske EU-formandskab 2025. Formål og målsætning Danmark skal fra den 1. juli til 31. december 2025 varetage det roterende formandskab for EU's ministerråd (EU-formandskabet). Det indebærer en omfattende række mødeaktiviteter på dansk jord herunder ministermøder, embedsmøder og –konferencer samt muligvis også topmøder med forventet deltagelse af mere end 17.000 personer. Møderne vil blive holdt på forskellige konferencesteder i Danmark og strække sig over 20-25 dage fordelt på 13 – 16 mødeblokke. Mødeaktiviteterne forventes at tiltrække mediebevågenhed, og formandskabet skal have en officiel leverandør af tv-tjenester – en host broadcaster. Host broadcasteren vil skulle levere tv-signaler samt tv-optagelser til de akkrediterede tv-stationer og på bestilling til andre tv-stationer af de større møder i Danmark. Forud for en konkurrenceudsættelse af HBC-opgaven åbner Udenrigsministeriet nu for en markedsdialog med potentielle leverandører af opgaven. Markedsdialogen forventes at foregå i perioden fra offentliggørelse af denne meddelelse og frem til 1. juni 2024, men med ønske om at modtage svar på Udenrigsministeriets spørgsmål senest den 1. maj 2024. Udenrigsministeriet ønsker med denne markedsdialog at modtage svar fra interesserede host broadcastere på en række spørgsmål med henblik på at fastlægge markedskonforme krav til ydelserne, herunder i forhold til tekniske forhold, vedlagsstruktur, kapaciteter mv.. Spørgsmålene fremgår under yderligere oplysninger i denne meddelelse. Interesserede host broadcastere kan også downloade et dokument med spørgsmålene via det elektroniske udbudssystem: https://eu.eu-supply.com/app/rfq/rwlentrance_s.asp?PID=395889&B= Udenrigsministeriet forbeholder sig retten til at indkalde interesserede host broadcastere til dialogmøde(r) med henblik på at drøfte Udenrigsministeriets spørgsmål. Udenrigsministeriet forbeholder sig endvidere retten til at udvide spørgerammen i løbet af dialogprocessen. Resultatet af Udenrigsministeriets markedsdialog sammenfattes i et notat, der offentliggøres i det elektroniske udbudssystem. Det anbefales, at interesserede host broadcastere løbende holder sig orienteret om markedsdialogen via det elektroniske udbudssystem. Kontaktpersoner Besvarelse af spørgsmål samt generelle henvendelser vedr. host broadcasting og EU-formandskabet kan ske via det elektroniske udbudssystem eller til EULOG@um.dk CC: Souschef Anne Louise Grinsted Klinkby Kontor for EU-formandskabslogistik anngri@um.dk og Chefkonsulent Europapolitisk kontor Louise Brincker: lobrin@um.dk Kort beskrivelse af opgaverne Kontrakten vil omfatte levering af HBC-ydelser til tv, radio og webcast herunder den nødvendige teknik, opstilling, montering og installation samt servicering og betjening af det benyttede udstyr. HBC-opgaven vil blandt andet indebære: - At etablere, producere og levere tv-dækning i lyd og billeder samt medieproduktionsmiljø under formandskabet til anvendelse af alle akkrediterede medier og på be-stilling fra medier. - At levere direkte transmission fra officielle pressekonferencer ved ministermøder samt evt. topmøder og ved Kommissionens besøg samt arrival og exit doorsteps til anvendelse af de akkrediterede tv-stationer til de pågældende møder. - At levere billed- og lydoptagelser af håndtryk, tour de table og familiefoto til akkrediterede tv-stationer på konferencestederne og på bestilling til andre tv-stationer - At levere den tekniske infrastruktur herunder forudsætningerne for input til CCTV og webcast og være ansvarlig for opsætning og nedtagning af teknisk udstyr. - At levere international og national distribution af direkte tv og optagelser på bestil-ling fra de bestillende tv-stationer. Signaler til de akkrediterede tv-stationers egne SNG-vogne skal leveres uden omkostninger for tv-stationerne. Den internationale og nationale distribution via satellit og kabel skal tilbydes på kommercielle vilkår.

title: Swath scanning laser altimeter
description: DTU Space is heavily involved in ESA’s airborne satellite calibration and validation campaigns in polar regions. To secure the DTU Space instrument package is living up to the needs for validation of current (ESA CryoSat, NASA ICESat-2) and to exploit the precision of future dual-frequency satellite missions (such as Copernicus high-priority candidate mission CRISTAL) it is of vital importance to purchase a swath scanning laser altimeter. The laser altimeter shall be a compact system adapted to a mid-sized aircraft and capable of measuring the surface of sea ice, land ice and ocean water. As the laser scanner system will be used together with airborne radar altimeters, the laser scanner shall, as a minimum, be operable within ranges of 300-1000 m for reflective targets of ≥ 10%. The purchase is a vital part of the nationally funded project Greenland Integrated Observing System (GIOS) and contributes to the development of a new research infrastructure providing a much-required sustained and long-term observation network of the central climate around Greenland representing not only entire Greenland but also a climate gradient representing the Arctic as a whole.

title: Laser Frequency Comb for 2ES
description: DTU will like to buy a Laser Frequency Comb for 2ES (The Second Earth Spectrograph). The Second Earth Spectrograph (2ES) is a next-generation extreme-precision radial velocity spectro-graph that will be installed at the MPG/ESO 2.2m Telescope on La Silla, Chile (Southern Hemisphere). 2ES will be dedicated to a > 5-year observing program with access to the majority (2/3) of the tele-scope time with the goal of discovering temperate terrestrial Earth-mass planets in the habitable zone around the brightest solar-type stars in the sky. In order to achieve the extreme precision needed for 2ES to complete its science objectives, a Laser Frequency Comb (LFC) calibration source is crucial in order to be able to calibrate the spectrograph to achieve the extreme precision of 10 cm/s over many years of operation. The LFC must cover the entire wavelength range of 2ES (370 nm to 870 nm) and have comb lines at appropriate spacing (see requirements) and have extreme stability (see requirements). The LFC must be able to function in a as-tronomical observing environment, be remotely operatable and be also to sustain a significant uptime at the astronomical telescope.

title: PreCommercial Procurement for the Customisation/Preoperationalisation of Water management Innovations from Space for European Climate Resilience
description: This PCP (Pre-Commercial Procurement) is a cross-border joint procurement of R&D services to reinforce public demand-driven innovation in end-user services in the area of Climate Change Adaptation through data-driven water management. The to-be-developed solutions are expected to achieve TRL 7-8. The PCP should deliver successful, innovative and fully tested product(s) and/or service(s) that meet the common needs of the Public Buyer Group (PBG) to procure research services, develop innovative marketable solutions, speed up the time-to-market and provide best value for money. More concretely, the common needs of the public buyer group are as follows. PCP WISE aims to develop smart, sustainable solutions to improve water management and climate resiliency by monitoring the ‘Soil-Water-Vegetation (SWV) System’. Market entities are challenged to design and develop a solution that achieves this by using and combining earth observation data and environmental data on the SWV-system. This to-be-developed integrated water intelligence information product/service aims to help decision-makers manage major challenges resulting from climate change, such as floods, droughts, wildfires, heat stress and infrastructure risks in both urban and rural areas. The PCP WISE project includes 5 use cases that serve as practical testing scenarios where innovative solutions must demonstrate their effectiveness in real-world conditions. They represent the diverse geographic and climatic contexts of the European continent that provide the reference framework against which the innovations are validated for relevance, resilience and impact. PCP WISE contractors are challenged by designing and developing a solution that is applicable and scalable to tackle all 5 use cases. Following the completion of the evaluation of the tenders received, the PCP has entered its implementation phase by means of awarding a Framework Agreement where contractors are developing the solution in competition. It includes call-offs for Specific Contracts for Phase 1: Solution Design, Phase 2: Prototype Development, and Phase 3: Validation and demonstration of the solutions. This project receives funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme under grant agreement number No. 101182917 and selected under the HORIZONCL62024 GOVERNANCE015, topic: Customisation/preoperationalisation of prototypes enduser services in the area Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation, with a budget of around €12 million earmarked for the R&D phases during the implementation of the PCP instrument. However, the European Union does not participate as a contracting authority in the procurement.
